On top of that, the singer 'RESCENE' performed at the festival yesterday, which seemed to draw even bigger crowds. All the restaurants I had initially looked up were packed, so while searching for a place that had a waiting system, I headed toward one of the spots on my backup list. About 40 minutes before arriving, I joined the remote waiting line via CatchTable, and even then, there were 74 teams ahead of me. Fortunately, it seemed quite a few guests gave up waiting, as the queue dropped significantly faster than expected. In fact, by the time we arrived, our turn was coming up so quickly that it made me a bit anxious. Luckily, we got there right around waiting number 8 and were able to walk right in with great timing. ```adcard ``` Although there is a dedicated parking lot right in front of the restaurant, it was impossible to park there due to the massive crowd of waiting customers and festival visitors. Instead, there was a parking attendant at the entrance, but his guidance felt somewhat unfriendly and hard to understand, which was a little disappointing. Still, there are several small public parking lots nearby, so we were able to park close by without much trouble. Looking at the size and operation of the restaurant, I could see why the long line moved so quickly. There is a separate imminent entry waiting area. When your number is called, you immediately place your order, pay up front, grab a water bottle and paper cups, and seat yourself at your assigned table. There were also plenty of outdoor tables, making the overall turnover rate look very efficient. ```adcard ``` We ordered one serving each of the Charcoal-Grilled Spicy Pork Plate and the Braised Cutlassfish. After a short wait, the side dishes were served first, dished out in very small portions just enough for a taste. You could freely refill whatever side dishes you needed at the self-service bar. Personally, I often feel bad about leftover food going to waste, so serving smaller portions initially seemed like quite a reasonable approach. The self-service bar also offers sungnyung (scorched rice tea), so you can grab some warm tea whenever you want. Considering how busy the place was, the food came out remarkably fast. The charcoal-grilled spicy pork was infused with rich smokiness and flavor from the grill, making it delicious, and the braised cutlassfish was neither excessively salty nor too spicy, suiting our palates well. However, the portion of meat felt a bit light by our standards, leaving us feeling that ordering two servings of the pork would have been better. Wrap vegetables were also available at the self-service bar, allowing us to bring as many as we needed to make wraps. Overall, it was a tasty, satisfying, and hearty meal with very little to complain about. ## Pictures
